paragraph: Dumont is a real seller's market right now. Fifty-one single-family homes sold at a median of $680,000, the sale-to-list ratio is 1.05, roughly 76 percent closed above asking, and the median days on market is 14. Sellers are dictating terms on well-presented houses, and the typical sale is a three-bedroom colonial, split-level, or cape with two full baths. The range runs from $468,500 to $940,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The monthly series backs the seasonal arc cleanly. Medians climbed from $650,000 in February to $699,000 in July, and July was the heaviest closing month at 15 sales. If Dumont follows the usual pattern, expect volume to taper modestly through fall and the median to drift back off that summer peak. Two-families are the smaller tier, eight sales at a median of $780,000 with 18 days on market, all of them true two-family properties with a median of four bedrooms. Eight sales is thin, so treat that number as a general level rather than a precise one. If you're weighing the two, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the rental income of a two-family.
